componentBoundAssumption: The separate draft study joins entries that share a primary publication. This is a conditional metadata bound, not a frozen leakage-graph result.
evidenceForDependence: All three entries cite the same primary DOI.
All three receptor-subunit sequence hashes match across entries, despite differences in descriptions and reference accessions.
Nb24 sequences share an identical 123-residue prefix; the longer deposited sequence adds HHHHHHEPEA.

constructObservations.fact: 9SLM contains Nb24 only; 9SL1 and 9SLD contain Nb24 and a deposited entity named Mb30.
constructObservations.inference: Do not describe all three as containing both binders.

constructObservations.fact: The deposited Mb30 entity is 138 residues long.
constructObservations.inference: Its name does not establish that the sequence represents the complete experimentally used megabody. Scaffold and construct completeness remain unresolved.

constructObservations.fact: The 133-residue Nb24 sequence equals the 123-residue 9SLM sequence followed by HHHHHHEPEA.
constructObservations.inference: The suffix is consistent with purification/detection tags, but its experimental provenance is unreviewed. No sequence is silently trimmed.

constructObservations.fact: 9SL1/9SLD alpha4 references P48169, while the identical 9SLM alpha4 sequence references F6UBA8 and Q9D6F4. Beta3/fusion descriptions also differ despite identical sequence hashes.
constructObservations.inference: Canonical receptor identity, species and engineered construct mapping require reconciliation before generation or evaluation.
